headline: High risk of shared-workspace data leakage and capability conflict; prompt-injection and cascading-error risks are medium.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat and semantica both read/write files, and semantica also ingests MCP resources and web/API content. If semantica consumes Mentat-produced files or diffs as trusted input, attacker-controlled text can steer downstream actions. The interaction is plausible from the profiles, though not directly documented.
conditions: IF semantica ingests Mentat-generated files, diffs, or notes as instructions without provenance checks
IF a shared filesystem or MCP resource is used as the bridge between the agents
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all Mentat outputs before semantica reads them
Require semantica to treat Mentat text as untrusted data by default
Separate input folders for each agent
Review any shared MCP resource permissions
requires-engineering: add content-signing or provenance enforcement

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read and write the filesystem, and Mentat explicitly handles model-provider API keys while semantica handles tokens, passwords, and private keys. Because their shared state is via filesystem and semantica can access many local and remote data sources, sensitive files can flow between them by default unless isolated.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or home directory
IF secrets are stored in files accessible to either agent
mitigations: Use separate workspaces per agent
Move secrets into per-agent vaults
Restrict file permissions on credential files
Disable shared mounts between the agents
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can modify git state and write the filesystem, and semantica can also modify git state, write the filesystem, and operate over a shared intelligence layer. With no locking mechanism stated, concurrent edits to the same repo or data directory can overwrite each other or corrupt state.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository or directory
IF no external lock or merge gate is present
mitigations: Assign disjoint repositories or directories
Serialize git writes through one operator
Use a lock file around shared mutable paths
Run dry-run diffs before applying changes
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals, while semantica has a shared context graph and deterministic infrastructure that can consume prior outputs. If semantica treats Mentat output as authoritative without verification, errors can propagate into knowledge graphs or decisions. The pathway is plausible but not shown as default action-taking.
conditions: IF semantica imports Mentat-generated diffs or summaries into its graph without validation
IF downstream workflows act on semantica's derived records
mitigations: Require human review before importing Mentat outputs
Validate Mentat outputs against source files
Keep derived records separate from raw edits
Add checksum or provenance checks on imported artifacts
requires-engineering: add verification gates before graph ingestion

E_compliance.rationale: Mentat is open-source and appears focused on source code, while semantica handles enterprise data, contracts, audit trails, and secrets. If the same regulated data is routed through both, semantica's broader data classes and secret handling create a retention/residency mismatch risk, but the profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction conflict.
conditions: IF regulated enterprise data or secrets are processed by both agents
IF their retention or residency policies differ for the same dataset
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to either agent
Keep regulated data out of Mentat workspaces
Document retention rules for semantica outputs
Review vendor/data-processing terms before deployment
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
